summary:
The DaVinci International Film Festival (DIFF) is an annual Los Angeles event founded in 2017 by filmmaker Chadwick Pelletier. It is produced by the DaVinci Film Society, a nonprofit recognized as a 501(c)(3) in 2019. The festival showcases independent features, shorts, animation, documentaries and screenplays, with Leo Awards for competition categories. Its programs include the Storyline screenplay competition, DaVinci Labs, ultra-short GENiUS and DIFFdocs.

DIFF held virtual editions in 2020 and 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic and returned to in-person screenings at The Grove in 2022. In 2024, it gave its inaugural Visionary Award to Michael J. Fox. The 2025 edition launched FilmAfrica, an initiative with Swahili Village Group to promote African cinema; a Nairobi awards platform is planned for 2026 with support from the Kenya Film Commission. That year, DIFF also held its first DaVinci Masquerade at Cannes.

The festival’s eighth edition took place in Los Angeles in September 2026, honoring writer-director Randall Wallace with its Visionary Award and introducing the RiseUP initiative.
